items.title: China dissented from G20 statement opposing 'cheap exports' flooding market, Bessent says
items.title_zh: China dissented from G20 statement opposing 'cheap exports' flooding market, Bessent says
items.summary: 未调用大模型，以下为原文关键信息摘录：China was the only Group of 20 member to dissent from a joint statement that "non-market based economies pushing out a never-ending stream of cheap exports is not sustainable," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday.；The other G20 members will take action in the coming "days, weeks or months" to "reach a resolution on this unsustainable equilibrium," Bessent said at a press conference following days of meetings with finance ministers and central bankers in Asheville, North Carolina.；The statement, released later Tuesday by the Treasury Department, includes a footnote specifying that China objected to a paragraph in which the 19 members agreed "that countries should take steps to eliminate non-market policies and practices that exacerbate imbalances." "In particular, countries with excessive and persistent external surpluses should remove distortions that constrain domestic consumption and that result in an overreliance on exports for growth," that paragraph reads.
important_points: China was the only Group of 20 member to dissent from a joint statement that "non-market based economies pushing out a never-ending stream of cheap exports is not sustainable," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday.

The other G20 members will take action in the coming "days, weeks or months" to "reach a resolution on this unsustainable equilibrium," Bessent said at a press conference following days of meetings with finance ministers and central bankers in Asheville, North Carolina.

The statement, released later Tuesday by the Treasury Department, includes a footnote specifying that China objected to a paragraph in which the 19 members agreed "that countries should take steps to eliminate non-market policies and practices that exacerbate imbalances." items.title_zh: Used cars under $20,000 tend to sell quickly — but there are trade-offs for buyers
items.summary: 未调用大模型，以下为原文关键信息摘录：It's still possible to find used cars for under $20,000 — but buyers may have to make bigger trade-offs than they did in the past.；About 32% of all used-car sales in the second quarter of 2026 were for vehicles under $20,000, down sharply from 55.2% for the same quarter in 2019, according to Edmunds, an auto research site.；The lower the price, the more quickly the vehicles sold: A used car in the $5,000 to $10,000 range spent an average 25.4 days on a dealer lot, compared with 37.8 days for vehicles costing $20,000 to $25,000 and 44.3 days for those priced at more than $50,000, according to Edmunds.

items.title: Hugging Face's new duck robot is selling fast. A Chinese chip powers it
items.title_zh: Hugging Face's new duck robot is selling fast. A Chinese chip powers it
items.summary: 未调用大模型，以下为原文关键信息摘录：BEIJING — A popular new programmable personal robot from a French-American company is powered by a chip from Shanghai-listed Rockchip which in turn uses British company ARM's tech, reflecting how intertwined global tech supply chains remain.；The colorful "Microduck" robot from Hugging Face's French subsidiary Pollen Robotics has sold more than 10,000 units since its launch on Thursday, with sales surpassing $5 million as of late Tuesday, according to Hugging Face.；That level of demand for the robot has quickly delayed delivery times for new orders past the initial promise of Christmas 2026.
important_points: BEIJING — A popular new programmable personal robot from a French-American company is powered by a chip from Shanghai-listed Rockchip which in turn uses British company ARM's tech, reflecting how intertwined global tech supply chains remain.

The colorful "Microduck" robot from Hugging Face's French subsidiary Pollen Robotics has sold more than 10,000 units since its launch on Thursday, with sales surpassing $5 million as of late Tuesday, according to Hugging Face.
That level of demand for the robot has quickly delayed delivery times for new orders past the initial promise of Christmas 2026.
